messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water is only **slightly above 0 °C**.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (slope ≈ –0.07 K / MPa), the temperature shift from 1 atm (101.3 kPa) to 10 kPa is:

\[
\Delta T \approx \left(-0.07\;\frac{\text{K}}{\text{MPa}}\right)\times(-91.3\;\text{kPa})
          \approx +0.0066\;\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point is roughly **0.006 °C** (≈ 0.01 °C) above the standard 0 °C. In practice this difference is negligible, so you can consider the freezing point to be **0 °C** under these conditions.

---

**Why the tool isn’t used**

The provided `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` function only calculates boiling points, not freezing points. Therefore, I calculated the freezing point manually using thermodynamic principles.
